behavior.arguments: rdi = base pointer; rsi = length; rdx = seed B; rcx = seed A; r8 = xor key. No field is written; the window only reads the buffer and returns a folded value.

edges.zero_length: n=0 -> bound zero -> return seedA ^ seedB (0x1111 ^ 0x2222 = 0x3333).
edges.short_length: n=5 (<16) -> bound zero -> same seed xor.
edges.single_step: n=16, mem=[1, 2], key=0, A=3, B=5 -> 6 (hand trace in README).
edges.far_chunk: n=32, mem=[1, 2, 3, 4], key=0, A=3, B=5 -> 8; one step over the far chunk, then the meeting guard exits.
edges.two_step_overlap: n=48, mem=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], key=0, A=3, B=5 -> 77; the second step re-reads the middle chunk from both streams.
edges.high_part: n=16, mem=[0, 3], key=0, A=all-ones, B=0 -> 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF6; the 128-bit product's high half folds into the result.

behavior.entry_shape: Straight-line setup, one loop with two forward branches (meeting guard, loop-back) plus the zero-bound entry branch, one ret; no call opcode inside the window.
behavior.return_rule: L = rsi & 0x7fffffffffffffff; if (rsi & 0x7ffffffffffffff0) == 0, return seedA ^ seedB. Else, with base2 = rdi + (rsi & 0xf), A = seedA, B = seedB, p = rdi, r11 = rsi & 0x7ffffffffffffff0: repeat { bound = base2 + r11; if p >= bound (unsigned) stop; A ^= [p+8]; (hi1, lo1) = ([bound-8] ^ key) * A; B ^= [p]; (hi2, lo2) = ([bound-16] ^ key) * B; A = hi1 ^ lo1; B = hi2 ^ lo2; p += 16; r11 -= 16 } until r11 == 0; return A ^ B. Multiplies are unsigned 64x64->128.
behavior.weakness: Heavy for the easy-packet bar: a loop with two 128-bit multiplies per step, not a single gate. The window is bound only because its full rule locks exactly from its own bytes and was re-verified against an independent byte-level emulator over 5,062 cases with zero mismatches (see reverification).
behavior.iteration_count: ceil(L/32) steps for L >= 16, else 0; the forward and backward streams may overlap near the meeting point.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; zero sites found. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.
incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_note: One R_X86_64_RELATIVE slot (0x57709e8, addend 0x16488e0) names the window; reported as a slot list, no meaning claimed.

reverification.method: Dev-time only (not part of the packet, which is stdlib-only): the window bytes were decoded with Capstone and executed by a small instruction interpreter (mov/movabs/and/lea/cmp/xor/mul/add/branches/ret, with ZF/CF tracking and a bounds-checked buffer) against the closed-form rule in the checker. The interpreter derives every operand from the Capstone decode, so it is independent of the rule's transcription; a misread register, displacement, or multiply order would surface as a mismatch. The emulator script is not committed (it needs Capstone, which is not stdlib); the 8 fixed vectors below were produced by the emulator and are replayed by the checker.
reverification.domain: Effective lengths 0..1024 exhaustive x 2 seed sets (2,050 runs); 3,000 random runs with effective length <= 2048 and edge seeds (0, 1, 2^64-1, 2^63, 0x8000000000000000, 0x7fffffffffffffff); 12 raw-length variants with bit 63 set (same effective length). Every run asserted all reads inside the effective-length buffer.

scout_corrections: The round-12 scout note listed this window (backup B2, the last unbuilt round-12 item) with FDE [0x16488e0, 0x1648946), 102 bytes, 10 padding bytes, zero direct callers, one naming slot 0x57709e8, and nearest claimed window three-way unsigned clamp 0x15e4f70 (packet #16) 0x63970 away. Every element verified exactly. Two phrasing points are reconciled explicitly: the scout's compressed per-step summary ('rcx ^= rax, r9 ^= r10') glosses the two mov steps (rcx = high half of the second product, then xor low half; r9 = high half of the first product, then xor low half) — the full register trace in the README is equivalent, not a correction. And the scout's 'zero calls' describes the window body (no call opcode inside it), while the incoming scan independently finds zero direct sites — the two statements agree. Unlike most packets, this window does NOT open with endbr64; its first instruction is mov %rcx,%r9.
